title: Publicity, advertising and the union
summary: Maxwell blames publicity and the union.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Well, you said earlier you were wondering what happened, you know, to our comparative salaries and everything, because in terms of what we used to make, a staff job should have been paid $900 a week or something, $1,000 a week. Now, the thing is that America is a country of supply and demand and we are not offering something -- we're not supplying something that's not in demand for what they want.

Now, the fault of that is that America is also a country that is ruled by advertisements and ad agency propaganda. Because you know, any dumb singer, you get the Mafia putting up a million bucks of advertising, and he's a hit overnight. So it's not a matter, even, of how good it is. It's just how well publicized it is. And we don't get any publicity for what we want to do.

The people who are interested in pushing American music generally are like these private, rich people we spoke about before, who will have their own private parties. But they're not dedicated enough -- I shouldn't expect them to be, either -- or rich enough, really, to put on an all out campaign.

Now, we've got a union, which you and I know is a joke. Our union could take some of those millions they've got in all these mysterious trustfunds they've got, and put on some kind of an advertising campaign. It's a matter of publicity.
Of awareness, sure. Let the people know.

Yeah, if we hired -- I bet you anything in the world, if we got one of these advertising agencies that some foreign dictators come over here and you give them $5 million and they make them look like the lion of the season, social season. If we got one of these big shot advertisers behind us, our union took some of this money of theirs, the mysterious money that they collect out of our salaries, and
put on a campaign, I think we could make them aware.
